title: Code graph and static dependency analysis
subtitle: The code graph under my memory service is extracted with a parser into partitioned edge tables; dependency traces are bounded database traversals with no model involved, and the explainer may narrate only proven edges.

lede: In FAFOHive, my agents had to know the blast radius of a symbol before changing it, and a language model asked for call paths invents some. tree-sitter extracts calls, imports, implements, references, definitions and re-exports from source, and they land in partitioned PostgreSQL edge tables. An edge whose endpoint is not indexed yet stays pending, and a resolver promotes it only once both endpoints are indexed. Graph generations let me rebuild an index without serving a half-built graph, and each request is pinned to one generation. trace symbol dependencies is plain traversal: a bounded breadth-first search in SQL with a Redis fast path, returning edges and nodes with file and line.
quote: Structure must come from a parser and a database; a model may only put that structure into words.
evidence: Static dependency analysis: a parser-built code graph of 6 edge kinds over a monorepo of ~19,000 files, covering 294,033 of 294,362 code chunks.
PostgreSQL graph traversal: dependency traces as bounded breadth-first searches in SQL with a Redis fast path and no model call.
Evidence-grounded LLM output: an explainer that hands a model only a path the code graph has proven, up to five hops.
author: Corey James
